questions.question: What happens when a solution of an acid is mixed with a solution of a base in a test tube?

options.text: The temperature of the solution decreases
The temperature of the solution remains the same
Salt formation takes place and the temperature increases

questions.explanation: The reaction between an acid and a base is a neutralization reaction which is exothermic (releases heat) and forms salt and water.

source.section: 2.2 What do all Acids and Bases have in common?

questions.question: Which of the following salts does not contain water of crystallization?
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO3) and does not contain water of crystallization. Blue vitriol (CuSO4.5H2O), washing soda (Na2CO3.10H2O), and gypsum (CaSO4.2H2O) all contain water of crystallization.

source.section: 2.4 Are the Crystals of Salts really Dry?

questions.question: An aqueous solution turns red litmus solution blue. Excess addition of which of the following solution would reverse the change?
questions.explanation: Turning red litmus blue indicates the original solution is basic. To reverse the change (turn it back to red), an acid must be added in excess. Hydrochloric acid is the only acid listed.

source.section: 2.1 Understanding the Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases

questions.question: What is the pH range of our body to work normally?
questions.explanation: Our body works within the pH range of 7.0 to 7.8. Living organisms can survive only in a narrow range of pH change.

source.section: 2.3 Importance of pH in Everyday Life

questions.question: Tooth decay starts when the pH of the mouth is lower than:
questions.explanation: Tooth decay starts when the pH of the mouth is lower than 5.5, as the acid produced by bacteria begins to corrode the tooth enamel.

source.section: 2.3 Importance of pH in Everyday Life
